title: Who, which, that: the man by the window
titleFa: مردی که کنار پنجره نشسته است
titleR: mard-i ke kenār-e panjare neshaste ast
intro: To describe people and things in detail – the man who is sitting by the window, the book I bought yesterday, the place where I work – Persian uses one little word, که, and one small ending, -i, on the noun before it. In this lesson you learn to build these relative clauses, to use the handy patterns کسی که (the person who), چیزی که (what) and جایی که (where), and to say 'whose' and 'with whom'. You also spend Yalda, the longest night of the year, with Leila's family.
goals: describe people and things with a relative clause: مردی که آن‌جا نشسته است
add the -i before که in all its spellings: مردی، خانه‌ای، آقایی
use کسی که، چیزی که، جایی که and هر چیزی که
say 'whose', 'with whom' and 'in which' with a pronoun inside the clause
know where را goes when a noun has a relative clause

sections.title: Who's who on Yalda night
sections.context: It is Yalda night, the longest night of the year. Leila has invited Tom to her grandparents' house, where the whole family has gathered.

lines.en: Leila, who's that man sitting by the window?
lines.col: لیلا، اون آقاهه که کنار پنجره نشسته کیه؟
lines.colR: Leylā, un āghā-he ke kenār-e panjare neshaste ki-ye?

lines.colV: لَیلا، اون آقاهه که کِنارِ پَنجَره نِشَسته کیه؟

lines.fa: او پدربزرگ من است؛ همان کسی که قبلاً معلم بود.

lines.fa: آهان! و خانمی که دارد چای می‌ریزد؟

lines.col: مامان‌بزرگمه؛ همون که همه‌ی این غذاها رو پخته.
lines.colR: māmān-bozorg-am-e; hamun ke hame-ye in ghazā-hā ro pokhte.
lines.faV: مادَربُزُرگَم اَست؛ کَسی که هَمه‌یِ این غَذاها را پُخته اَست.
lines.colV: مامان‌بُزُرگَمه؛ هَمون که هَمه‌یِ این غَذاها رو پُخته.

lines.fa: غذاهایش عالی است! آن دختری که با گربه بازی می‌کند خواهرت است؟

lines.col: آره! یه صدایی داره که آدمو جادو می‌کنه.
lines.colR: āre! ye sedā-yi dāre ke ādam-o jādu mi-kone.
lines.faV: بَله! صِدایی دارَد که آدَم را جادو می‌کُنَد.

lines.fa: آجیل شب یلداست. هر چیزی که دوست داری بردار!
lines.r: ājil-e shab-e Yaldā-st. har chiz-i ke dust dāri bardār!
lines.en: It's Yalda-night nuts. Take whatever you like!
lines.col: آجیل شب یلداست. هر چی دوست داری بردار!
lines.colR: ājil-e shab-e Yaldā-st. har chi dust dāri bardār!
lines.faV: آجیلِ شَبِ یَلداست. هَر چیزی که دوست داری بَردار!
lines.colV: آجیلِ شَبِ یَلداست. هَر چی دوست داری بَردار!

lines.fa: ممنون. این اولین شب یلدایی است که در ایران هستم.
lines.r: mamnun. in avvalin shab-e Yaldā-yi ast ke dar Irān hastam.
lines.en: Thank you. This is the first Yalda night I've spent in Iran.
lines.col: مرسی. این اولین شب یلداییه که ایرانم.
lines.colR: mersi. in avvalin shab-e Yaldā-yi-ye ke Irān-am.
lines.faV: مَمنون. این اَوَّلین شَبِ یَلدایی اَست که دَر ایران هَستَم.
lines.colV: مِرسی. این اَوَّلین شَبِ یَلداییه که ایرانَم.

lines.fa: پس باید فال حافظ بگیری! این کاری است که همه در شب یلدا می‌کنند.
lines.r: pas bāyad fāl-e Hāfez begiri! in kār-i ast ke hame dar shab-e Yaldā mi-konand.
lines.en: Then you must have your fortune read from Hafez! It's something everyone does on Yalda night.
lines.col: پس باید فال حافظ بگیری! این کاریه که همه شب یلدا می‌کنن.
lines.colR: pas bāyad fāl-e Hāfez begiri! in kār-i-ye ke hame shab-e Yaldā mi-konan.

sections.title: Describing with که

items.note: one word for people and things

ex.fa: دوستی که در شیراز دارم معلم است.
ex.r: dust-i ke dar Shirāz dāram mo'allem ast.
ex.en: The friend I have in Shiraz is a teacher.
ex.faV: دوستی که دَر شیراز دارَم مُعَلِّم اَست.

ex.fa: کسی که زنگ زد برادرت بود.
ex.r: kas-i ke zang zad barādar-at bud.
ex.en: The person who rang was your brother.
ex.faV: کَسی که زَنگ زَد بَرادَرَت بود.

items.note: همان کسی که 'the very person who, the one who'
Persian has a word for each kind of cousin: دخترعمو، پسرعمو، دخترخاله، پسرخاله، دختردایی…
present stem نشین neshin; نشسته است 'is sitting' (literally 'has sat')
also 'reader' – from خواندن 'to read; to sing'
فال گرفتن 'to have your fortune told'
literally 'it came to my memory'; the opposite of یادم رفت 'I forgot'

ex.en: You look a lot like your mother.

items.note: مو 'hair' is usually plural in Persian: موهایش 'her hair'

sections.title: An old wedding photo
sections.intro: Leila shows Tom an old photo from her parents' wedding. Almost every sentence has a relative clause – find the noun with -i and the که that follows it.

sections.title: Yalda, the longest night
sections.md:
On the night of 20 or 21 December – the last night of autumn and the longest of the year – Iranian families gather for [[شب یلدا|shab-e Yaldā]], also called [[شب چله|shab-e chelle]]. People go to the home of the oldest relatives, usually the grandparents, and sit up late, talking, eating and reading poetry, keeping each other company through the long dark until the sun is 'born again'. The name *Yaldā* comes from a Syriac word meaning *birth*.

The table has its own menu: red fruits that stand for the dawn and the warmth of life – [[هندوانه|hendevāne|watermelon]], which is said to keep winter illness away, and [[انار|anār|pomegranate]] – with bowls of [[آجیل|ājil]], nuts and dried fruit. Late in the evening someone takes down the Divan of Hafez for a [[فال حافظ|fāl-e Hāfez]]: you make a silent wish, open the book at random, and the ghazal on that page is read aloud as the poet's answer.

sections.title: Watch out
items: **که** is used for people and things alike – Persian has no separate *who* and *which*.

Don't forget the **-i**: *mard-i ke…* 'the man who…', not *mard ke…*. A name or a pronoun takes no -i: *Leylā, ke…* 'Leila, who…'. In speech, Tehranis often use the 'that one' ending *-e* instead: *un dokhtar-e ke…* 'that girl who…'.
The verb comes at the end of the relative clause, so two verbs often meet: *ketāb-i ke kharidam gom shod* 'the book I bought got lost'. Read such a sentence in two parts.
In careful writing را stays with its noun: *ketāb-i rā ke kharidi khāndam*; in speech it moves after the clause: *ketābi ke kharidi ro khundam*.
For *whose* and *with whom*, put a pronoun inside the clause: *dokhtar-i ke esm-ash…* 'the girl whose name…', *kas-i ke bā u…* 'the person with whom…'.
